title: Bootstrap‐Based Forecasting for Locally Stationary Long‐Memory Processes: An Application to Daily PM2.5$$ {\mathrm{PM}}_{2.5} $$ Concentrations in Coyhaique, Chile
content:
ABSTRACT

Forecasting is a central objective in time series analysis, with increasing interest in obtaining accurate predictions and reliable prediction intervals. State-space models provide a natural framework for this purpose through the Kalman filter, although conventional predictive inference often relies on Gaussian innovations and time-invariant system matrices. We propose a state-space bootstrap (SSB) procedure for constructing prediction intervals that accommodates time-varying system matrices, incorporates parameter estimation uncertainty through bootstrap reestimation, and relaxes the Gaussian assumption by resampling standardized innovations. The methodology is applied to daily PM2.5$$ {\mathrm{PM}}_{2.5} $$ concentrations in Coyhaique, Chile, using a regression–LSARFIMA(1,d(u),0)$$ \mathrm{LSARFIMA}\left(1,d(u),0\right) $$ model formulated within the SS framework. The systematic component accounts for trend and annual seasonality through Fourier harmonics, while the stochastic component captures short- and long-range dependence, allowing the fractional memory parameter d(u)$$ d(u) $$ and innovation scale σ(u)$$ \sigma (u) $$ to evolve smoothly over time.
